newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australia bonds sit tight, key week awaits.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australia bonds sit tight, key week awaits.

text.p: *Australian bond futures held little changed during the pre-weekend SYCOM session, while jittery U.S. Treasuries weakened ahead of a key week for both markets.
*Australian Q2 inflation and wages data due this week.
Australian bond futures held little changed during the pre-weekend SYCOM session in the face of a jittery U.S. Treasury market.

The September 10-year bond futures contract ended after-hours trade unchanged from Friday's soft pit close at 93.400, but will be looking to retest last week's 3-1/2 year SYCOM high of 93.510 should this week's data outcomes go to plan.

Median forecasts for Wednesday's second quarter headline CPI centre on a 0.1 percent fall for an annual rate of 0.5 percent, while the underlying inflation rate is seen up 0.4 percent for a year-on-year 1.7 percent, according to a Reuters survey.
This would be below the Reserve Bank's 2.0-3.0 percent target for the policy sensitive underlying rate.

Thursday's annual average weekly ordinary time earnings are also expected to be contained below the central bank's 4.5 percent "line in the sand" with the quarterly rate rising 0.8 percent for 4.1 percent growth.

Such outcomes are expected to reinforce calls for an easing in current 5.5 percent official interest rates and could prompt the 10-year contract to take out the 93.510 contract peak for an attack on the all time high of 93.630.

However, some analysts stress that the 10-year contract is already nearing overbought levels again with a relative strength index close to 75 percent, although it does remain below the extreme plus-80 percent level seen earlier this month.
Initial support is pegged at 93.360, they added.

Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries were taking a cautious line on Friday ahead of its key event this week, Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Tuesday and Wednesday.
The U.S. 30-year bond yield crept back above 6.50 percent on Friday.
